**Victor Mugubi Wanyama** ([Kenyan English](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenyan_English "Kenyan English"):[[waˈɲama]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA "Help:IPA")[](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/transcoded/c/c3/Victor_Mugubi_Wanyama.ogg/Victor_Mugubi_Wanyama.ogg.mp3 "Play audio")[ⓘ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Victor_Mugubi_Wanyama.ogg "File:Victor Mugubi Wanyama.ogg"); born 25 June 1991) is a Kenyan former professional [footballer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football "Association football") who played as a [defensive midfielder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Defensive_midfielder "Defensive midfielder").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wanyama#cite_note-Captain-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wanyama#cite_note-5)

Wanyama became the first ever Kenyan player to score in the [UEFA Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Champions_League "UEFA Champions League") when he scored the first goal in [Celtic's 2–1 win over FC Barcelona on 7 November 2012](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celtic_F.C._2%E2%80%931_FC_Barcelona "Celtic F.C. 2–1 FC Barcelona").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wanyama#cite_note-6) On 11 July 2013, he moved to [Premier League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Premier_League "Premier League") club [Southampton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southampton_F.C. "Southampton F.C.") for £12.5 million, making him the most expensive player sold by a Scottish club at the time, surpassing the £9.5 million Russian club [Spartak Moscow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Spartak_Moscow "FC Spartak Moscow") paid for [Aiden McGeady](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aiden_McGeady "Aiden McGeady") in 2010.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wanyama#cite_note-7) In summer 2016, Wanyama moved to Southampton's Premier League rivals [Tottenham Hotspur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tottenham_Hotspur_F.C. "Tottenham Hotspur F.C."), reaching the [2019 UEFA Champions League final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_UEFA_Champions_League_final "2019 UEFA Champions League final") with the side, before signing for [Major League Soccer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Soccer "Major League Soccer") club [CF Montréal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CF_Montr%C3%A9al "CF Montréal") in March 2020. In 2025, Wanyama returned to Scotland to play for [Dunfermline Athletic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dunfermline_Athletic_F.C. "Dunfermline Athletic F.C.") under his former Celtic manager [Neil Lennon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neil_Lennon "Neil Lennon").

After making his international debut for the [Kenya national team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_national_football_team "Kenya national football team") in May 2007 at the age of 15, Wanyama went on to earn over 60 caps for the country, and represented them at the [2019 Africa Cup of Nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Africa_Cup_of_Nations "2019 Africa Cup of Nations").

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Victor_Wanyama&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Wanyama attended Kamukunji High School, known for its successful football team. After High School, he played for JMJ Academy for three years and joined [Kenyan Premier League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenyan_Premier_League "Kenyan Premier League") clubs [Nairobi City Stars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi_City_Stars "Nairobi City Stars") and [AFC Leopards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AFC_Leopards "AFC Leopards").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wanyama#cite_note-Cement-8) In 2007, he joined [Allsvenskan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allsvenskan "Allsvenskan") club [Helsingborg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Helsingborgs_IF "Helsingborgs IF"), but returned to Kenya in 2008 after his brother, [McDonald Mariga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McDonald_Mariga "McDonald Mariga"), moved to [Serie A](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serie_A "Serie A") side [Parma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parma_F.C. "Parma F.C.").

During his childhood, he was a fan of [Celtic F.C.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celtic_F.C. "Celtic F.C."), and would watch the club's matches from a local club modelled on Celtic called [Kibera Celtic](https://facebook.com/groups/240070772832231/).[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wanyama#cite_note-youtube.com-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wanyama#cite_note-10)

## Club career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Victor_Wanyama&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Club career")]

### Beerschot AC

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Victor_Wanyama&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Beerschot AC")]

After a successful trial, Wanyama signed for [Beerschot AC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K._Beerschot_AC "K. Beerschot AC") on a four-year contract in summer 2008. He made his debut in a League match at the end of the [2008–09 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008%E2%80%9309_Belgian_First_Division "2008–09 Belgian First Division"). In September 2009, he was fined €100 and given a three-match suspension for a violent tackle on [Matías Suárez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mat%C3%ADas_Su%C3%A1rez "Matías Suárez") of [Anderlecht](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R.S.C._Anderlecht "R.S.C. Anderlecht").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wanyama#cite_note-11)

In the summer of 2010 [Scottish Premier League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scottish_Premier_League "Scottish Premier League") club [Celtic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celtic_F.C. "Celtic F.C.") attempted to sign Wanyama but Beerschot did not allow him to leave. Russian club [CSKA Moscow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CSKA_Moscow "CSKA Moscow") also attempted to sign him, but they failed as well.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wanyama#cite_note-12)

Wanyama scored his first goal for Beerschot on 11 December 2010, a 77th-minute equaliser against Westerlo. In April 2011, he received another three match suspension after video evidence showed he had elbowed Brecht Dejaeghere of [K.V. Kortrijk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K.V._Kortrijk "K.V. Kortrijk").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wanyama#cite_note-13)

### Celtic

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Victor_Wanyama&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Celtic")]

[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6b/Victor_Wanyama_2012.jpg/250px-Victor_Wanyama_2012.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Victor_Wanyama_2012.jpg)

Wanyama playing for [Celtic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celtic_F.C. "Celtic F.C.") in 2012

On 9 July 2011, Wanyama finally completed a £900,000 move to Celtic, after the Scottish club had failed to sign him the previous year.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wanyama#cite_note-Celtic-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wanyama#cite_note-15) He signed a four-year contract and in doing so became the first ever Kenyan to play in the SPL. Wanyama chose 67 as his squad number to honour the [Lisbon Lions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lisbon_Lions "Lisbon Lions"), Celtic's [1967 European Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1967_European_Cup_Final "1967 European Cup Final")-winning team.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wanyama#cite_note-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wanyama#cite_note-17)

Wanyama made his Celtic league debut in a 1–0 loss to [St Johnstone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St_Johnstone_F.C. "St Johnstone F.C.") on 21 August 2011. He played in central defence rather than his favoured central midfield role.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wanyama#cite_note-18) He came on as a late substitute in a 4–0 win over [Motherwell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Motherwell_F.C. "Motherwell F.C."),[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wanyama#cite_note-19) and played for the whole second half in a 2–0 [League Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scottish_League_Cup "Scottish League Cup") win over [Ross County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ross_County_F.C. "Ross County F.C.").[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wanyama#cite_note-20) On 29 September 2011, he started in Celtic's 1–1 draw with Italian team [Udinese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Udinese_Calcio "Udinese Calcio") in the [Europa League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Europa_League "Europa League"). This was his first European match for the club.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wanyama#cite_note-21) On 10 December 2011, Wanyama scored his first goal for Celtic in a 1–0 win over [Hearts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heart_of_Midlothian_F.C. "Heart of Midlothian F.C.") at [Celtic Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celtic_Park "Celtic Park"), a tremendous 25-yard strike which hit the top corner.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wanyama#cite_note-22) His performances during December earned him the [Scottish Premier League young player of the month](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scottish_Premier_League_monthly_awards "Scottish Premier League monthly awards") award.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wanyama#cite_note-23) He scored his second Celtic goal on 2 January 2012 in a 3–0 win against Dunfermline at [East End Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_End_Park "East End Park").[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wanyama#cite_note-24) Wanyama scored in Celtic's 2–1 win against [Dundee United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dundee_United_F.C. "Dundee United F.C.") at [Celtic Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celtic_Park "Celtic Park")[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wanyama#cite_note-25) and in the 4–0 victory against [Hearts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hearts_F.C. "Hearts F.C.") at [Tynecastle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tynecastle_Stadium "Tynecastle Stadium").[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wanyama#cite_note-26)

On 20 October 2012, Wanyama scored twice against [St Mirren](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St_Mirren_F.C. "St Mirren F.C.") at [St Mirren Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St_Mirren_Park "St Mirren Park"), the second of which was a half volley from 25 yards out.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wanyama#cite_note-27) On 25 October, Wanyama's agent released a statement saying that he had turned down an improved contract offer from [Celtic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celtic_F.C. "Celtic F.C."), stating that his wage demands could not be met by the club amid speculation of interest from clubs in England.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wanyama#cite_note-28) On 7 November, Wanyama opened the scoring with a powerful header as [Celtic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celtic_F.C. "Celtic F.C.") shocked [Barcelona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Barcelona "FC Barcelona") in the [Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Champions_League "UEFA Champions League") group stage, by beating them [2–1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celtic_F.C._2%E2%80%931_FC_Barcelona "Celtic F.C. 2–1 FC Barcelona") at [Celtic Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celtic_Park "Celtic Park").[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wanyama#cite_note-29)

Wanyama received a nomination for the [PFA Scotland Young Player of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PFA_Scotland_Young_Player_of_the_Year "PFA Scotland Young Player of the Year") for [2012–13](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012%E2%80%9313_in_Scottish_football "2012–13 in Scottish football"),[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wanyama#cite_note-30) but the winner was announced as [Leigh Griffiths](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leigh_Griffiths "Leigh Griffiths")[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wanyama#cite_note-31)

### Southampton

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Victor_Wanyama&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Southampton")]

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d1/Victor_Wanyama_2014.jpg/250px-Victor_Wanyama_2014.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Victor_Wanyama_2014.jpg)

Wanyama with [Southampton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southampton_F.C. "Southampton F.C.") in 2014

After much speculation and a previous breakdown in talks, on 11 July 2013, Wanyama signed for [Premier League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Premier_League "Premier League") side [Southampton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southampton_F.C. "Southampton F.C.") for a fee claimed to be £12.5 million,[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wanyama#cite_note-32) making him the first Kenyan to ever play in the Premier League.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wanyama#cite_note-33)

Wanyama said:

> Southampton is a good club and it has good players, so I just want to train hard and work hard to be a part of the starting XI. We'll see where that will take me. It feels great and I am happy to be here. There were other options, but Southampton is a club with ambitions so I chose to come here. I'm very grateful to be here and I'm looking forward to playing in the Premier League.

He made his debut on 17 August 2013, in a 1–0 away win against [West Bromwich Albion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Bromwich_Albion_F.C. "West Bromwich Albion F.C.").[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wanyama#cite_note-34) Wanyama made 24 appearances in his first season, but injuries hindered his efforts to make much of an impact in the team.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wanyama#cite_note-35)

Under new manager [Ronald Koeman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronald_Koeman "Ronald Koeman"), Wanyama came into his own in the 2014–15 season.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wanyama#cite_note-f411-36) He scored his first goal for the club in a 1–0 [league](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014%E2%80%9315_Premier_League "2014–15 Premier League") victory over [Swansea City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swansea_City_F.C. "Swansea City F.C.") at the [Liberty Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liberty_Stadium "Liberty Stadium") on 20 September 2014, after replacing [James Ward-Prowse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Ward-Prowse "James Ward-Prowse") in the 69th minute.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wanyama#cite_note-37) His next goal came in an 8–0 trouncing of [Sunderland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunderland_A.F.C. "Sunderland A.F.C.") on 19 October 2014.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wanyama#cite_note-38) Wanyama would score his third goal for the Saints in spectacular fashion, a 40-yard shot after [Eldin Jakupović](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eldin_Jakupovi%C4%87 "Eldin Jakupović")'s poor clearance fell straight to him, in what proved to be the only goal in a win over [Hull City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hull_City_A.F.C. "Hull City A.F.C.").[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wanyama#cite_note-39) His performances saw him awarded the league's African Player of the Month for September,[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wanyama#cite_note-f411-36) with him stating "It is wonderful being recognised as someone who has done well for his club."[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wanyama#cite_note-f411-36)

### Tottenham Hotspur

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Victor_Wanyama&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Tottenham Hotspur")]

[![Image 7](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c7/Manchester_United_v_Tottenham_Hotspur%2C_December_2016_%2808%29.JPG/250px-Manchester_United_v_Tottenham_Hotspur%2C_December_2016_%2808%29.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Manchester_United_v_Tottenham_Hotspur,_December_2016_(08).JPG)

Wanyama _(left)_ alongside Spurs clubmates in a league clash with [Manchester United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester_United_F.C. "Manchester United F.C.") in 2016

On 23 June 2016, Premier League club [Tottenham Hotspur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tottenham_Hotspur_F.C. "Tottenham Hotspur F.C.") announced that they had reached an agreement with Southampton for the transfer of Wanyama,[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wanyama#cite_note-40) signing a five-year contract for a fee of £11 million.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wanyama#cite_note-41) Wanyama had previously worked with Tottenham manager [Mauricio Pochettino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mauricio_Pochettino "Mauricio Pochettino") who brought him to Southampton in July 2013.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wanyama#cite_note-42) Wanyama scored his first goal for the club on his home debut against [Crystal Palace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crystal_Palace_F.C. "Crystal Palace F.C."), in the 82nd minute of a 1–0 league win for Spurs.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wanyama#cite_note-43) The goal made him the 138th different player to score for the club, extending its record for the most variety of goalscorers for a single club in the Premier League.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wanyama#cite_note-44)

Early in the [2017–18](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017%E2%80%9318_Tottenham_Hotspur_F.C._season "2017–18 Tottenham Hotspur F.C. season") season, Wanyama injured his knee in the match against Chelsea and was sidelined for over four months.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wanyama#cite_note-45) He returned to training in mid-December.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wanyama#cite_note-46)[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wanyama#cite_note-47) On 2 January 2018, he made his first appearance after his injury, as a substitute in the away match against [Swansea City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swansea_City_A.F.C. "Swansea City A.F.C.").[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wanyama#cite_note-48) His equaliser in Tottenham's 2–2 draw with [Liverpool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liverpool_F.C. "Liverpool F.C.") on 4 February 2018 was voted the Premier League Goal of the Month.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wanyama#cite_note-49)

Wanyama picked up a knee injury in a pre-season game of the [2018–19 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Tottenham_Hotspur_F.C._season "2018–19 Tottenham Hotspur F.C. season") against Barcelona.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wanyama#cite_note-50) He made his first start of the season two months later in the [EFL Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_EFL_Cup "2018–19 EFL Cup") game against [Watford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Watford_F.C. "Watford F.C.") that Spurs won on penalties.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wanyama#cite_note-51) At the end of August 2019 Tottenham had agreed to sell Wanyama to [Club Brugge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Club_Brugge "Club Brugge") for £13 million, however Wanyama had "concerns over the move" and the deal broke down.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wanyama#cite_note-52)

### CF Montréal

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Victor_Wanyama&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: CF Montréal")]

On 3 March 2020, Tottenham announced that it had agreed to transfer Wanyama to [Major League Soccer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Soccer "Major League Soccer") club Montreal Impact, where he would become a [Designated Player](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Designated_Player "Designated Player").[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wanyama#cite_note-53)[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wanyama#cite_note-54)

On 11 March 2020, Wanyama made his competitive debut for Montreal at [Stade Olympique](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stade_Olympique "Stade Olympique") in the first leg of a quarterfinal in the [CONCACAF Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CONCACAF_Champions_League "CONCACAF Champions League"), where he was named in manager [Thierry Henry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thierry_Henry "Thierry Henry")'s starting side. Wanyama provided an assist to [Saphir Taïder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saphir_Ta%C3%AFder "Saphir Taïder") – with whom Wanyama was (despite Saphir not playing a single game for the Saints) briefly teammates at Southampton in 2014 – in a 1–2 defeat by Honduran champions [C.D. Olimpia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C.D._Olimpia "C.D. Olimpia").[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wanyama#cite_note-55)[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wanyama#cite_note-56)

On 21 November 2021, the midfielder [captained](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Captain_(association_football) "Captain (association football)") his side to a 1–0 victory over [Toronto FC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toronto_FC "Toronto FC") in the [2021 Canadian Championship Final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Canadian_Championship_Final "2021 Canadian Championship Final").[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wanyama#cite_note-57)

In October 2022, Wanyama initially announced that he would not renew his contract with CF Montréal at the end of the season.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wanyama#cite_note-58) However, in January 2023, he was officially re-signed by the Canadian club, signing a new two-year contract.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wanyama#cite_note-59)[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wanyama#cite_note-60)[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wanyama#cite_note-61)

### Dunfermline Athletic

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Victor_Wanyama&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Dunfermline Athletic")]

On 26 March 2025, Wanyama joined [Scottish Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scottish_Championship "Scottish Championship") club [Dunfermline Athletic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dunfermline_Athletic_F.C. "Dunfermline Athletic F.C.") on a short-term deal until the end of the season, reuniting with his former [Celtic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celtic_F.C. "Celtic F.C.") manager and new Dunfermline manager [Neil Lennon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neil_Lennon "Neil Lennon").[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wanyama#cite_note-62)[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wanyama#cite_note-63) Three days later, he made his debut in a 3–0 loss against [Ayr United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ayr_United "Ayr United") where he was sent off in the 84th minute for a [handball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Handball_(soccer) "Handball (soccer)") offence.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wanyama#cite_note-64)

On 3 April 2026, Wanyama announced his retirement from professional football.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wanyama#cite_note-65)

## International career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Victor_Wanyama&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: International career")]

Wanyama made his debut for the [Kenyan senior national team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_national_football_team "Kenya national football team") in May 2007, aged just 15, in a friendly against [Nigeria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nigeria_national_football_team "Nigeria national football team").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wanyama#cite_note-Cement-8) He went on play in all six of Kenya's [2010 FIFA World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_FIFA_World_Cup "2010 FIFA World Cup")[qualifiers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_FIFA_World_Cup_qualification_(CAF) "2010 FIFA World Cup qualification (CAF)").

Having first become the [captain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Captain_(association_football) "Captain (association football)") of the _Harambee Stars_ in 2013,[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] he represented Kenya at the [2019 Africa Cup of Nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Africa_Cup_of_Nations "2019 Africa Cup of Nations").[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wanyama#cite_note-66)

In September 2021, after being repeatedly overlooked for selection during the [2022 FIFA World Cup qualifiers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup_qualification "2022 FIFA World Cup qualification"), Wanyama announced his retirement from international football, marking the end of his 14-year duty.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wanyama#cite_note-67) However, following the [FKF](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Football_Kenya_Federation "Football Kenya Federation")'s re-admission in global competitions by [FIFA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIFA "FIFA") and a personal meeting with Kenya's Sports Minister at the time, [Ababu Namwamba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ababu_Namwamba "Ababu Namwamba"), in December 2022 the midfielder officially agreed to restore his eligibility for the senior national team, together with [Michael Olunga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Olunga "Michael Olunga").[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wanyama#cite_note-68)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Victor_Wanyama&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Wanyama comes from a sporting family. His brother [McDonald Mariga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McDonald_Mariga "McDonald Mariga") was also a professional footballer,[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wanyama#cite_note-69)[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wanyama#cite_note-70) while his other brothers [Thomas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_Wanyama "Thomas Wanyama") and [Sylvester](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylvester_Wanyama?action=edit&redlink=1 "Sylvester Wanyama (page does not exist)") are also footballers in the [Kenyan Premier League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenyan_Premier_League "Kenyan Premier League"). His father, Noah Wanyama, was a footballer for [A.F.C. Leopards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A.F.C._Leopards "A.F.C. Leopards") in the 1980s,[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wanyama#cite_note-71) and his sister [Mercy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercy_Wanyama "Mercy Wanyama") is a professional basketball player in Spain.

Wanyama is managed by [ExtraTime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rob_Moore_(South_African_Entrepreneur)?action=edit&redlink=1 "Rob Moore (South African Entrepreneur) (page does not exist)"),[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wanyama#cite_note-ETVic-72) and has a boot sponsorship deal with [Adidas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adidas "Adidas").

In 2015, Wanyama participated in the production of a short film about football in Kenya called _Mdudu Boy_, written and directed by actress [Ella Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ella_Smith_(actress) "Ella Smith (actress)").[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wanyama#cite_note-73)

In December 2022, Wanyama was key in urging then [CF Montréal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CF_Montr%C3%A9al "CF Montréal") teammate and friend [Alistair Johnston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alistair_Johnston "Alistair Johnston") to move to his former club [Celtic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celtic_F.C. "Celtic F.C."). Johnston has credited Wanyama with the move, jokingly referring to him as "agent Victor".[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wanyama#cite_note-youtube.com-9)

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

(Redirected from [Parse](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Parse&redirect=no "Parse"))

Analysing a string of symbols, according to the rules of a formal grammar

"Parse" redirects here. For other uses, see [Parse (disambiguation)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parse_(disambiguation) "Parse (disambiguation)").

**Parsing**, **syntax analysis**, or **syntactic analysis** is a process of analyzing a [string](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/String_(computer_science) "String (computer science)") of [symbols](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Symbol_(formal) "Symbol (formal)"), either in [natural language](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natural_language "Natural language"), [computer languages](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer_languages "Computer languages") or [data structures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Data_structure "Data structure"), conforming to the rules of a [formal grammar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Formal_grammar "Formal grammar") by breaking it into parts. The term _parsing_ comes from Latin _pars_ (_orationis_), meaning [part (of speech)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Part_of_speech "Part of speech").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parse?search=played%20seven%20seasons%20Premier%20League#cite_note-dictionary.com-1)

The term has slightly different meanings in different branches of [linguistics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linguistics "Linguistics") and [computer science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer_science "Computer science"). Traditional [sentence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sentence_(linguistics) "Sentence (linguistics)") parsing is often performed as a method of understanding the exact meaning of a sentence or word, sometimes with the aid of devices such as [sentence diagrams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sentence_diagram "Sentence diagram"). It usually emphasizes the importance of grammatical divisions such as [subject](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subject_(grammar) "Subject (grammar)") and [predicate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Predicate_(grammar) "Predicate (grammar)").

Within [computational linguistics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computational_linguistics "Computational linguistics") the term is used to refer to the formal analysis by a computer of a sentence or other string of words into its constituents, resulting in a [parse tree](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parse_tree "Parse tree") showing their syntactic relation to each other, which may also contain [semantic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Semantics "Semantics") information.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] Some parsing algorithms generate a _parse forest_ or list of parse trees from a string that is [syntactically ambiguous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syntactic_ambiguity "Syntactic ambiguity").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parse?search=played%20seven%20seasons%20Premier%20League#cite_note-Tomita2012-2)

The term is also used in [psycholinguistics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Psycholinguistics "Psycholinguistics") when describing language comprehension. In this context, parsing refers to the way that human beings analyze a sentence or phrase (in spoken language or text) "in terms of grammatical constituents, identifying the parts of speech, syntactic relations, etc."[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parse?search=played%20seven%20seasons%20Premier%20League#cite_note-dictionary.com-1) This term is especially common when discussing which linguistic cues help speakers interpret [garden-path sentences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garden_path_sentence "Garden path sentence").

Within computer science, the term is used in the analysis of [computer languages](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer_languages "Computer languages"), referring to the syntactic analysis of the input code into its component parts in order to facilitate the writing of [compilers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Compilers "Compilers") and [interpreters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interpreter_(computing) "Interpreter (computing)"). The term may also be used to describe a split or separation.

In data analysis, the term is often used to refer to a process extracting desired information from data, e.g., creating a [time series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_series "Time series") signal from a [XML](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/XML "XML") document.

## Human languages

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Parsing&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Human languages")]

Main category: [Natural language parsing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Category:Natural_language_parsing "Category:Natural language parsing")

### Traditional methods

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Parsing&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Traditional methods")]

The traditional grammatical exercise of parsing, sometimes known as _clause analysis_, involves breaking down a text into its component [parts of speech](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Part_of_speech "Part of speech") with an explanation of the form, function, and syntactic relationship of each part.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parse?search=played%20seven%20seasons%20Premier%20League#cite_note-3) This is determined in large part from study of the language's [conjugations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conjugation_(grammar) "Conjugation (grammar)") and [declensions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Declensions "Declensions"), which can be quite intricate for heavily [inflected](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inflection "Inflection") languages. To parse a phrase such as "man bites dog" involves noting that the [singular](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammatical_number "Grammatical number") noun "man" is the [subject](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subject_(grammar) "Subject (grammar)") of the sentence, the verb "bites" is the [third person singular](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammatical_person "Grammatical person") of the [present tense](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Present_tense "Present tense") of the verb "to bite", and the singular noun "dog" is the [object](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Object_(grammar) "Object (grammar)") of the sentence. Techniques such as [sentence diagrams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sentence_diagram "Sentence diagram") are sometimes used to indicate relation between elements in the sentence.

Parsing was formerly central to the teaching of grammar throughout the English-speaking world, and widely regarded as basic to the use and understanding of written language.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

### Computational methods

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Parsing&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Computational methods")]

Main article: [Syntactic parsing (computational linguistics)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syntactic_parsing_(computational_linguistics) "Syntactic parsing (computational linguistics)")

[![Image 4: icon](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/9/99/Question_book-new.svg/60px-Question_book-new.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Question_book-new.svg)This section **needs [more citations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Verifiability "Wikipedia:Verifiability")**. Please help [improve this section](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special:EditPage/Parsing "Special:EditPage/Parsing") by [adding citations to reliable sources](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Referencing_for_beginners "Help:Referencing for beginners"). Unsourced material may be challenged and [removed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Verifiability#Burden_of_evidence "Wikipedia:Verifiability")._(February 2013)_ _([Learn how and when to remove this message](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Maintenance\_template\_removal "Help:Maintenance template removal"))_

In some [machine translation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Machine_translation "Machine translation") and [natural language processing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natural_language_processing "Natural language processing") systems, written texts in human languages are parsed by computer programs.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parse?search=played%20seven%20seasons%20Premier%20League#cite_note-ManningManning1999-4) Human sentences are not easily parsed by programs, as there is substantial [ambiguity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syntactic_ambiguity "Syntactic ambiguity") in the structure of human language, whose usage is to convey meaning (or [semantics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Semantics "Semantics")) amongst a potentially unlimited range of possibilities, but only some of which are germane to the particular case.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parse?search=played%20seven%20seasons%20Premier%20League#cite_note-5) So an utterance "Man bites dog" versus "Dog bites man" is definite on one detail but in another language might appear as "Man dog bites" with a reliance on the larger context to distinguish between those two possibilities, if indeed that difference was of concern. It is difficult to prepare formal rules to describe informal behaviour even though it is clear that some rules are being followed.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

In order to parse natural language data, researchers must first agree on the [grammar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammar "Grammar") to be used. The choice of syntax is affected by both [linguistic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Language "Language") and computational concerns; for instance some parsing systems use [lexical functional grammar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lexical_functional_grammar "Lexical functional grammar"), but in general, parsing for grammars of this type is known to be [NP-complete](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NP-complete "NP-complete"). [Head-driven phrase structure grammar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Head-driven_phrase_structure_grammar "Head-driven phrase structure grammar") is another linguistic formalism which has been popular in the parsing community, but other research efforts have focused on less complex formalisms such as the one used in the Penn [Treebank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treebank "Treebank"). [Shallow parsing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shallow_parsing "Shallow parsing") aims to find only the boundaries of major constituents such as noun phrases. Another popular strategy for avoiding linguistic controversy is [dependency grammar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dependency_grammar "Dependency grammar") parsing.

Most modern parsers are at least partly statistical; that is, they rely on a [corpus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Text_corpus "Text corpus") of training data which has already been annotated (parsed by hand). This approach allows the system to gather information about the frequency with which various constructions occur in specific contexts. _(See [machine learning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Machine\_learning "Machine learning").)_ Approaches which have been used include straightforward [PCFGs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PCFG "PCFG") (probabilistic context-free grammars),[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parse?search=played%20seven%20seasons%20Premier%20League#cite_note-6)[maximum entropy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maximum_entropy_classifier "Maximum entropy classifier"),[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parse?search=played%20seven%20seasons%20Premier%20League#cite_note-7) and [neural nets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neural_net "Neural net").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parse?search=played%20seven%20seasons%20Premier%20League#cite_note-8) Most of the more successful systems use _lexical_ statistics (that is, they consider the identities of the words involved, as well as their [part of speech](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Part_of_speech "Part of speech")). However such systems are vulnerable to [overfitting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Overfitting "Overfitting") and require some kind of [smoothing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smoothing "Smoothing") to be effective.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

Parsing algorithms for natural language cannot rely on the grammar having 'nice' properties as with manually designed grammars for programming languages. As mentioned earlier some grammar formalisms are very difficult to parse computationally; in general, even if the desired structure is not [context-free](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Context-free_language "Context-free language"), some kind of context-free approximation to the grammar is used to perform a first pass. Algorithms which use context-free grammars often rely on some variant of the [CYK algorithm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CYK_algorithm "CYK algorithm"), usually with some [heuristic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heuristic_(computer_science) "Heuristic (computer science)") to prune away unlikely analyses to save time. _(See [chart parsing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chart\_parsing "Chart parsing").)_ However some systems trade speed for accuracy using, e.g., linear-time versions of the [shift-reduce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shift-reduce_parsing "Shift-reduce parsing") algorithm. A somewhat recent development has been [parse reranking](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parse_reranking?action=edit&redlink=1 "Parse reranking (page does not exist)") in which the parser proposes some large number of analyses, and a more complex system selects the best option.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] In [natural language understanding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natural_language_understanding "Natural language understanding") applications, [semantic parsers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Semantic_parsing "Semantic parsing") convert the text into a representation of its meaning.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parse?search=played%20seven%20seasons%20Premier%20League#cite_note-:0-9)

### Psycholinguistics

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Parsing&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Psycholinguistics")]

In [psycholinguistics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Psycholinguistics "Psycholinguistics"), parsing involves not just the assignment of words to categories (formation of ontological insights), but the evaluation of the meaning of a sentence according to the rules of syntax drawn by inferences made from each word in the sentence (known as [connotation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Connotation "Connotation")). This normally occurs as words are being heard or read.

Neurolinguistics generally understands parsing to be a function of working memory, meaning that parsing is used to keep several parts of one sentence at play in the mind at one time, all readily accessible to be analyzed as needed. Because the human working memory has limitations, so does the function of sentence parsing.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parse?search=played%20seven%20seasons%20Premier%20League#cite_note-10) This is evidenced by several different types of syntactically complex sentences that demonstrate potential issues for mental parsing of sentences.

The first, and perhaps most well-known, type of sentence that challenges parsing ability is the garden-path sentence. These sentences are designed so that the most common interpretation of the sentence appears grammatically faulty, but upon further inspection, these sentences are grammatically sound. Garden-path sentences are difficult to parse because they contain a phrase or a word with more than one meaning, often their most typical meaning being a different part of speech.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parse?search=played%20seven%20seasons%20Premier%20League#cite_note-doi.org-11) For example, in the sentence, "the horse raced past the barn fell", raced is initially interpreted as a past tense verb, but in this sentence, it functions as part of an adjective phrase.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parse?search=played%20seven%20seasons%20Premier%20League#cite_note-12) Since parsing is used to identify parts of speech, these sentences challenge the parsing ability of the reader.

Another type of sentence that is difficult to parse is an attachment ambiguity, which includes a phrase that could potentially modify different parts of a sentence, and therefore presents a challenge in identifying syntactic relationship (i.e. "The boy saw the lady with the telescope", in which the ambiguous phrase with the telescope could modify the boy saw or the lady.) [[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parse?search=played%20seven%20seasons%20Premier%20League#cite_note-doi.org-11)

A third type of sentence that challenges parsing ability is center embedding, in which phrases are placed in the center of other similarly formed phrases (i.e. "The rat the cat the man hit chased ran into the trap".) Sentences with 2 or in the most extreme cases 3 center embeddings are challenging for mental parsing, again because of ambiguity of syntactic relationship.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parse?search=played%20seven%20seasons%20Premier%20League#cite_note-13)

Within neurolinguistics there are multiple theories that aim to describe how parsing takes place in the brain. One such model is a more traditional generative model of sentence processing, which theorizes that within the brain there is a distinct module designed for sentence parsing, which is preceded by access to lexical recognition and retrieval, and then followed by syntactic processing that considers a single syntactic result of the parsing, only returning to revise that syntactic interpretation if a potential problem is detected.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parse?search=played%20seven%20seasons%20Premier%20League#cite_note-14) The opposing, more contemporary model theorizes that within the mind, the processing of a sentence is not modular, or happening in strict sequence. Rather, it poses that several different syntactic possibilities can be considered at the same time, because lexical access, syntactic processing, and determination of meaning occur in parallel in the brain. In this way these processes are integrated.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parse?search=played%20seven%20seasons%20Premier%20League#cite_note-15)

Although there is still much to learn about the neurology of parsing, studies have shown evidence that several areas of the brain might play a role in parsing. These include the left anterior temporal pole, the left inferior frontal gyrus, the left superior temporal gyrus, the left superior frontal gyrus, the right posterior cingulate cortex, and the left angular gyrus. Although it has not been absolutely proven, it has been suggested that these different structures might favor either phrase-structure parsing or dependency-structure parsing, meaning different types of parsing could be processed in different ways which have yet to be understood.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parse?search=played%20seven%20seasons%20Premier%20League#cite_note-16)

### Parser

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Parsing&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Parser")]

"Parser" redirects here. For the scripting language named Parser, see [Parser (programming language)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parser_(programming_language) "Parser (programming language)").

A **parser** is a software component that takes input data (typically text) and builds a [data structure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Data_structure "Data structure") – often some kind of [parse tree](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parse_tree "Parse tree"), [abstract syntax tree](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abstract_syntax_tree "Abstract syntax tree") or other hierarchical structure, giving a structural representation of the input while checking for correct syntax. The parsing may be preceded or followed by other steps, or these may be combined into a single step. The parser is often preceded by a separate [lexical analyser](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lexical_analysis "Lexical analysis"), which creates tokens from the sequence of input characters; alternatively, these can be combined in [scannerless parsing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scannerless_parsing "Scannerless parsing"). Parsers may be programmed by hand or may be automatically or semi-automatically generated by a [parser generator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parser_generator "Parser generator"). Parsing is complementary to [templating](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Templating_language "Templating language"), which produces formatted _output._ These may be applied to different domains, but often appear together, such as the [scanf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scanf "Scanf")/[printf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Printf "Printf") pair, or the input (front end parsing) and output (back end code generation) stages of a [compiler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Compiler "Compiler").

The input to a parser is typically text in some [computer language](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer_language "Computer language"), but may also be text in a natural language or less structured textual data, in which case generally only certain parts of the text are extracted, rather than a parse tree being constructed. Parsers range from very simple functions such as [scanf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scanf "Scanf"), to complex programs such as the frontend of a [C++ compiler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C++_compiler "C++ compiler") or the [HTML](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HTML "HTML") parser of a [web browser](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Web_browser "Web browser"). An important class of simple parsing is done using [regular expressions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regular_expression "Regular expression"), in which a group of regular expressions defines a [regular language](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regular_language "Regular language") and a regular expression engine automatically generating a parser for that language, allowing [pattern matching](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pattern_matching "Pattern matching") and extraction of text. In other contexts regular expressions are instead used prior to parsing, as the lexing step whose output is then used by the parser.

The use of parsers varies by input. In the case of data languages, a parser is often found as the file reading facility of a program, such as reading in HTML or [XML](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/XML "XML") text; these examples are [markup languages](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Markup_language "Markup language"). In the case of [programming languages](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Programming_language "Programming language"), a parser is a component of a [compiler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Compiler "Compiler") or [interpreter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interpreter_(computing) "Interpreter (computing)"), which parses the [source code](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Source_code "Source code") of a [computer programming language](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer_programming_language "Computer programming language") to create some form of internal representation; the parser is a key step in the [compiler frontend](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Compiler_frontend "Compiler frontend"). Programming languages tend to be specified in terms of a [deterministic context-free grammar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deterministic_context-free_grammar "Deterministic context-free grammar") because fast and efficient parsers can be written for them. For compilers, the parsing itself can be done in one pass or multiple passes – see [one-pass compiler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One-pass_compiler "One-pass compiler") and [multi-pass compiler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multi-pass_compiler "Multi-pass compiler").

The implied disadvantages of a one-pass compiler can largely be overcome by adding [fix-ups](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Relocation_(computing) "Relocation (computing)"), where provision is made for code relocation during the forward pass, and the fix-ups are applied backwards when the current program segment has been recognized as having been completed. An example where such a fix-up mechanism would be useful would be a forward GOTO statement, where the target of the GOTO is unknown until the program segment is completed. In this case, the application of the fix-up would be delayed until the target of the GOTO was recognized. Conversely, a backward GOTO does not require a fix-up, as the location will already be known.

Context-free grammars are limited in the extent to which they can express all of the requirements of a language. Informally, the reason is that the memory of such a language is limited. The grammar cannot remember the presence of a construct over an arbitrarily long input; this is necessary for a language in which, for example, a name must be declared before it may be referenced. More powerful grammars that can express this constraint, however, cannot be parsed efficiently. Thus, it is a common strategy to create a relaxed parser for a context-free grammar which accepts a superset of the desired language constructs (that is, it accepts some invalid constructs); later, the unwanted constructs can be filtered out at the [semantic analysis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Semantic_analysis_(compilers) "Semantic analysis (compilers)") (contextual analysis) step.

For example, in [Python](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Python_(programming_language) "Python (programming language)") the following is syntactically valid code:

x: int = 1
print(x)

The following code, however, is syntactically valid in terms of the context-free grammar, yielding a syntax tree with the same structure as the previous, but violates the semantic rule requiring variables to be initialized before use:

x: int = 1
print(y)

### Overview of process

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Parsing&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Overview of process")]

[![Image 6: Flow of data in a typical parser](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/a/a9/Parser_Flow.gif?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail_unscaled)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Parser_Flow.gif "Flow of data in a typical parser")

Flow of data in a typical parser

The following example demonstrates the common case of parsing a computer language with two levels of grammar: lexical and syntactic.

The first stage is the token generation, or [lexical analysis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lexical_analysis "Lexical analysis"), by which the input character stream is split into meaningful symbols defined by a grammar of [regular expressions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regular_expression "Regular expression"). For example, a calculator program would look at an input such as "`12 * (3 + 4)^2`" and split it into the tokens `12`, `*`, `(`, `3`, `+`, `4`, `)`, `^`, `2`, each of which is a meaningful symbol in the context of an arithmetic expression. The lexer would contain rules to tell it that the characters `*`, `+`, `^`, `(` and `)` mark the start of a new token, so meaningless tokens like "`12*`" or "`(3`" will not be generated.

The next stage is parsing or syntactic analysis, which is checking that the tokens form an allowable expression. This is usually done with reference to a [context-free grammar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Context-free_grammar "Context-free grammar") which recursively defines components that can make up an expression and the order in which they must appear. However, not all rules defining programming languages can be expressed by context-free grammars alone, for example type validity and proper declaration of identifiers. These rules can be formally expressed with [attribute grammars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Attribute_grammar "Attribute grammar").

The final phase is [semantic parsing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Semantic_analysis_(computer_science) "Semantic analysis (computer science)") or analysis, which is working out the implications of the expression just validated and taking the appropriate action.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parse?search=played%20seven%20seasons%20Premier%20League#cite_note-17) In the case of a calculator or interpreter, the action is to evaluate the expression or program; a compiler, on the other hand, would generate some kind of code. Attribute grammars can also be used to define these actions.

## Types of parsers

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Parsing&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Types of parsers")]

The _task_ of the parser is essentially to determine if and how the input can be derived from the start symbol of the grammar. This can be done in essentially two ways:

[Top-down parsing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Top-down_parsing "Top-down parsing")Top-down parsing can be viewed as an attempt to find left-most derivations of an input-stream by searching for [parse trees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parse_tree "Parse tree") using a top-down expansion of the given [formal grammar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Formal_grammar "Formal grammar") rules. Tokens are consumed from left to right. Inclusive choice is used to accommodate [ambiguity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ambiguity "Ambiguity") by expanding all alternative right-hand-sides of grammar rules.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parse?search=played%20seven%20seasons%20Premier%20League#cite_note-AhoSethiUllman_1986-18) This is known as the primordial soup approach. Very similar to sentence diagramming, primordial soup breaks down the constituencies of sentences.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parse?search=played%20seven%20seasons%20Premier%20League#cite_note-19)[Bottom-up parsing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bottom-up_parsing "Bottom-up parsing")A parser can start with the input and attempt to rewrite it to the start symbol. Intuitively, the parser attempts to locate the most basic elements, then the elements containing these, and so on. [LR parsers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LR_parser "LR parser") are examples of bottom-up parsers. Another term used for this type of parser is [Shift-Reduce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shift-reduce_parser "Shift-reduce parser") parsing.
[LL parsers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LL_parser "LL parser") and [recursive-descent parser](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recursive-descent_parser "Recursive-descent parser") are examples of top-down parsers that cannot accommodate [left recursive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Left_recursion "Left recursion")[production rules](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Formal_grammar#The_syntax_of_grammars "Formal grammar"). Although it has been believed that simple implementations of top-down parsing cannot accommodate direct and indirect left-recursion and may require exponential time and space complexity while parsing [ambiguous context-free grammars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ambiguous_grammar "Ambiguous grammar"), more sophisticated algorithms for top-down parsing have been created by Frost, Hafiz, and Callaghan[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parse?search=played%20seven%20seasons%20Premier%20League#cite_note-FrostHafizCallaghan_2007-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parse?search=played%20seven%20seasons%20Premier%20League#cite_note-FrostHafizCallaghan_2008-21) which accommodate [ambiguity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ambiguity "Ambiguity") and [left recursion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Left_recursion "Left recursion") in polynomial time and which generate polynomial-size representations of the potentially exponential number of parse trees. Their algorithm is able to produce both left-most and right-most derivations of an input with regard to a given [context-free grammar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Context-free_grammar "Context-free grammar").

An important distinction with regard to parsers is whether a parser generates a _leftmost derivation_ or a _rightmost derivation_ (see [context-free grammar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Context-free_grammar "Context-free grammar")). LL parsers will generate a leftmost [derivation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parse_tree "Parse tree") and LR parsers will generate a rightmost derivation (although usually in reverse).[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parse?search=played%20seven%20seasons%20Premier%20League#cite_note-AhoSethiUllman_1986-18)

Some _graphical parsing_ algorithms have been designed for [visual programming languages](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Visual_programming_languages "Visual programming languages").[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parse?search=played%20seven%20seasons%20Premier%20League#cite_note-22)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parse?search=played%20seven%20seasons%20Premier%20League#cite_note-23) Parsers for visual languages are sometimes based on [graph grammars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graph_grammar "Graph grammar").[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parse?search=played%20seven%20seasons%20Premier%20League#cite_note-24)

[Adaptive parsing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adaptive_parsing "Adaptive parsing") algorithms have been used to construct "self-extending" [natural language user interfaces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natural_language_user_interface "Natural language user interface").[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parse?search=played%20seven%20seasons%20Premier%20League#cite_note-Lehman2012-25)

### Implementation

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Parsing&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Implementation")]

A simple parser implementation reads the entire input file, performs an intermediate computation or translation, and then writes the entire output file, such as in-memory [multi-pass compilers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multi-pass_compiler "Multi-pass compiler").

Alternative parser implementation approaches:

*   **push parsers** call registered handlers ([callbacks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Callback_(computer_programming) "Callback (computer programming)")) as soon as the parser detects relevant tokens in the input stream. A push parser may skip parts of the input that are irrelevant (an example is [Expat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Expat_(software) "Expat (software)")).
*   **pull parsers**, such as parsers that are typically used by [compilers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Compilers "Compilers") front-ends by "pulling" input text.
*   **incremental parsers** (such as incremental [chart parsers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chart_parser "Chart parser")) that, as the text of the file is edited by a user, does not need to completely re-parse the entire file.
*   **Active** versus **passive parsers**[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parse?search=played%20seven%20seasons%20Premier%20League#cite_note-26)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parse?search=played%20seven%20seasons%20Premier%20League#cite_note-27)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Parsing&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Lookahead")]

[C](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C_(programming_language) "C (programming language)") program that cannot be parsed with less than 2 token lookahead. _Top:_ C grammar excerpt.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parse?search=played%20seven%20seasons%20Premier%20League#cite_note-28)_Bottom:_ a parser has digested the tokens "`int v;main(){`" and is about to choose a rule to derive _Stmt_. Looking only at the first lookahead token "`v`", it cannot decide which of both alternatives for _Stmt_ to choose; the latter requires peeking at the second token.

Lookahead establishes the maximum incoming tokens that a parser can use to decide which rule it should use. Lookahead is especially relevant to [LL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LL_parser "LL parser"), [LR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LR_parser "LR parser"), and [LALR parsers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LALR_parser "LALR parser"), where it is often explicitly indicated by affixing the lookahead to the algorithm name in parentheses, such as LALR(1).

Most [programming languages](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Programming_language "Programming language"), the primary target of parsers, are carefully defined in such a way that a parser with limited lookahead, typically one, can parse them, because parsers with limited lookahead are often more efficient. One important change[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] to this trend came in 1990 when [Terence Parr](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terence_Parr "Terence Parr") created [ANTLR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ANTLR "ANTLR") for his Ph.D. thesis, a [parser generator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parser_generator "Parser generator") for efficient LL(_k_) parsers, where _k_ is any fixed value.

LR parsers typically have only a few actions after seeing each token. They are shift (add this token to the stack for later reduction), reduce (pop tokens from the stack and form a syntactic construct), end, error (no known rule applies) or conflict (does not know whether to shift or reduce).

Lookahead has two advantages.[_[clarification needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Please\_clarify "Wikipedia:Please clarify")_]

*   It helps the parser take the correct action in case of conflicts. For example, parsing the if statement in the case of an else clause.
*   It eliminates many duplicate states and eases the burden of an extra stack. A C language non-lookahead parser will have around 10,000 states. A lookahead parser will have around 300 states.

Example: Parsing the Expression 1 + 2 * 3[_[dubious](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Accuracy\_dispute#Disputed\_statement "Wikipedia:Accuracy dispute")–[discuss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talk:Parsing#Dubious "Talk:Parsing")_]

Set of expression parsing rules (called grammar) is as follows,
Rule1:E → E + E Expression is the sum of two expressions.
Rule2:E → E * E Expression is the product of two expressions.
Rule3:E → number Expression is a simple number
Rule4:+ has less precedence than *

Most programming languages (except for a few such as APL and Smalltalk) and algebraic formulas give higher precedence to multiplication than addition, in which case the correct interpretation of the example above is 1 + (2 * 3). Note that Rule4 above is a semantic rule. It is possible to rewrite the grammar to incorporate this into the syntax. However, not all such rules can be translated into syntax.

Simple non-lookahead parser actions
Initially Input = [1, +, 2, *, 3]

1.   Shift "1" onto stack from input (in anticipation of rule3). Input = [+, 2, *, 3] Stack = [1]
2.   Reduces "1" to expression "E" based on rule3. Stack = [E]
3.   Shift "+" onto stack from input (in anticipation of rule1). Input = [2, *, 3] Stack = [E, +]
4.   Shift "2" onto stack from input (in anticipation of rule3). Input = [*, 3] Stack = [E, +, 2]
5.   Reduce stack element "2" to Expression "E" based on rule3. Stack = [E, +, E]
6.   Reduce stack items [E, +, E] and new input "E" to "E" based on rule1. Stack = [E]
7.   Shift "*" onto stack from input (in anticipation of rule2). Input = [3] Stack = [E,*]
8.   Shift "3" onto stack from input (in anticipation of rule3). Input = [] (empty) Stack = [E, *, 3]
9.   Reduce stack element "3" to expression "E" based on rule3. Stack = [E, *, E]
10.   Reduce stack items [E, *, E] and new input "E" to "E" based on rule2. Stack = [E]

The parse tree and resulting code from it is not correct according to language semantics.

To correctly parse without lookahead, there are three solutions:

*   The user has to enclose expressions within parentheses. This often is not a viable solution.
*   The parser needs to have more logic to backtrack and retry whenever a rule is violated or not complete. The similar method is followed in LL parsers.
*   Alternatively, the parser or grammar needs to have extra logic to delay reduction and reduce only when it is absolutely sure which rule to reduce first. This method is used in LR parsers. This correctly parses the expression but with many more states and increased stack depth.

Lookahead parser actions[_[clarification needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Please\_clarify "Wikipedia:Please clarify")_]
1.   Shift 1 onto stack on input 1 in anticipation of rule3. It does not reduce immediately.
2.   Reduce stack item 1 to simple Expression on input + based on rule3. The lookahead is +, so we are on path to E +, so we can reduce the stack to E.
3.   Shift + onto stack on input + in anticipation of rule1.
4.   Shift 2 onto stack on input 2 in anticipation of rule3.
5.   Reduce stack item 2 to Expression on input * based on rule3. The lookahead * expects only E before it.
6.   Now stack has E + E and still the input is *. It has two choices now, either to shift based on rule2 or reduction based on rule1. Since * has higher precedence than + based on rule4, we shift * onto stack in anticipation of rule2.
7.   Shift 3 onto stack on input 3 in anticipation of rule3.
8.   Reduce stack item 3 to Expression after seeing end of input based on rule3.
9.   Reduce stack items E * E to E based on rule2.
10.   Reduce stack items E + E to E based on rule1.

The parse tree generated is correct and simply more efficient[_[clarification needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Please\_clarify "Wikipedia:Please clarify")_][_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] than non-lookahead parsers. This is the strategy followed in [LALR parsers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LALR_parser "LALR parser").

*   [CYK algorithm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CYK_algorithm "CYK algorithm"): an O(n 3) algorithm for parsing [context-free grammars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Context-free_grammar "Context-free grammar") in [Chomsky normal form](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chomsky_normal_form "Chomsky normal form")

*   [GLR parser](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GLR_parser "GLR parser"): an algorithm for parsing any [context-free grammar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Context-free_grammar "Context-free grammar") by [Masaru Tomita](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Masaru_Tomita "Masaru Tomita"). It is tuned for deterministic grammars, on which it performs almost [linear time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linear_time "Linear time") and O(n 3) in worst case.[_[clarification needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Please\_clarify "Wikipedia:Please clarify")_]

*   [LR parser](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LR_parser "LR parser"): A more complex [linear time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linear_time "Linear time") parsing algorithm for a larger class of [context-free grammars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Context-free_grammar "Context-free grammar"). From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

(Redirected from [Parse](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Parse&redirect=no "Parse"))

Analysing a string of symbols, according to the rules of a formal grammar

"Parse" redirects here. For other uses, see [Parse (disambiguation)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parse_(disambiguation) "Parse (disambiguation)").

**Parsing**, **syntax analysis**, or **syntactic analysis** is a process of analyzing a [string](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/String_(computer_science) "String (computer science)") of [symbols](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Symbol_(formal) "Symbol (formal)"), either in [natural language](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natural_language "Natural language"), [computer languages](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer_languages "Computer languages") or [data structures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Data_structure "Data structure"), conforming to the rules of a [formal grammar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Formal_grammar "Formal grammar") by breaking it into parts. The term _parsing_ comes from Latin _pars_ (_orationis_), meaning [part (of speech)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Part_of_speech "Part of speech").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parse?search=played%20seven%20seasons%20Premier%20League#cite_note-dictionary.com-1)

The term has slightly different meanings in different branches of [linguistics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linguistics "Linguistics") and [computer science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer_science "Computer science"). Traditional [sentence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sentence_(linguistics) "Sentence (linguistics)") parsing is often performed as a method of understanding the exact meaning of a sentence or word, sometimes with the aid of devices such as [sentence diagrams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sentence_diagram "Sentence diagram"). It usually emphasizes the importance of grammatical divisions such as [subject](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subject_(grammar) "Subject (grammar)") and [predicate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Predicate_(grammar) "Predicate (grammar)").

Within [computational linguistics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computational_linguistics "Computational linguistics") the term is used to refer to the formal analysis by a computer of a sentence or other string of words into its constituents, resulting in a [parse tree](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parse_tree "Parse tree") showing their syntactic relation to each other, which may also contain [semantic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Semantics "Semantics") information.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] Some parsing algorithms generate a _parse forest_ or list of parse trees from a string that is [syntactically ambiguous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syntactic_ambiguity "Syntactic ambiguity").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parse?search=played%20seven%20seasons%20Premier%20League#cite_note-Tomita2012-2)

The term is also used in [psycholinguistics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Psycholinguistics "Psycholinguistics") when describing language comprehension. In this context, parsing refers to the way that human beings analyze a sentence or phrase (in spoken language or text) "in terms of grammatical constituents, identifying the parts of speech, syntactic relations, etc."[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parse?search=played%20seven%20seasons%20Premier%20League#cite_note-dictionary.com-1) This term is especially common when discussing which linguistic cues help speakers interpret [garden-path sentences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garden_path_sentence "Garden path sentence").

Within computer science, the term is used in the analysis of [computer languages](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer_languages "Computer languages"), referring to the syntactic analysis of the input code into its component parts in order to facilitate the writing of [compilers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Compilers "Compilers") and [interpreters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interpreter_(computing) "Interpreter (computing)"). The term may also be used to describe a split or separation.

In data analysis, the term is often used to refer to a process extracting desired information from data, e.g., creating a [time series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_series "Time series") signal from a [XML](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/XML "XML") document.

## Human languages

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Parsing&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Human languages")]

Main category: [Natural language parsing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Category:Natural_language_parsing "Category:Natural language parsing")

### Traditional methods

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Parsing&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Traditional methods")]

The traditional grammatical exercise of parsing, sometimes known as _clause analysis_, involves breaking down a text into its component [parts of speech](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Part_of_speech "Part of speech") with an explanation of the form, function, and syntactic relationship of each part.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parse?search=played%20seven%20seasons%20Premier%20League#cite_note-3) This is determined in large part from study of the language's [conjugations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conjugation_(grammar) "Conjugation (grammar)") and [declensions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Declensions "Declensions"), which can be quite intricate for heavily [inflected](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inflection "Inflection") languages. To parse a phrase such as "man bites dog" involves noting that the [singular](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammatical_number "Grammatical number") noun "man" is the [subject](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subject_(grammar) "Subject (grammar)") of the sentence, the verb "bites" is the [third person singular](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammatical_person "Grammatical person") of the [present tense](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Present_tense "Present tense") of the verb "to bite", and the singular noun "dog" is the [object](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Object_(grammar) "Object (grammar)") of the sentence. Techniques such as [sentence diagrams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sentence_diagram "Sentence diagram") are sometimes used to indicate relation between elements in the sentence.

Parsing was formerly central to the teaching of grammar throughout the English-speaking world, and widely regarded as basic to the use and understanding of written language.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]
